name: Move the decimal
rule: Times 10, 100, 1000: slide the decimal right one place per zero. Divide: slide it left.
why: Our number system is built on tens. Multiplying by 10 makes every digit worth ten times more, so each digit shifts one place left of the decimal point, which looks like the point moving right.
workbookSection: Decimals; Unit 2 money and rate problems

clues: {p} has {k} zero{s}, so slide the decimal {k} place{s} right. Where does it land?
{p} has {k} zero{s}, so slide the decimal {k} place{s} left. Where does it land?
